title: How to change cursor in PowerPoint on Mac: guide for better visibility and presentations
metaTitle: How to change cursor in PowerPoint on Mac (2026)
description: Learn how to change cursor in PowerPoint on Mac during presentations or editing. Follow our guide to improve visibility and control your slide show experience.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: You cannot permanently change the default mouse cursor style within the PowerPoint application on your Mac. You can, however, use the built-in laser pointer tool during a presentation or adjust system-wide cursor settings in macOS to improve visibility.
tldr: PowerPoint does not support custom cursor themes or shapes.
Use the built-in laser pointer during slideshows by holding the Option key.
Change your cursor size and color in macOS System Settings for better visibility.
Third-party apps can provide extra cursor effects if needed.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor inside PowerPoint

Many users want to change the cursor to a different shape or color for presentations. PowerPoint for Mac does not have a native setting for this. The application relies on the standard macOS cursor. This design choice keeps the interface consistent with other Apple apps. If you need a specific cursor style for accessibility, you must change it at the system level.
How to use the built-in laser pointer
The most effective way to highlight content is the laser pointer. This tool turns your mouse into a red, green, or blue dot. It is perfect for drawing attention to specific data points on a slide.

items: Start your presentation in Slide Show mode.
Move your mouse to the bottom left corner of the screen.
Click the Pen or Pointer icon.
Select Laser Pointer from the menu.

blocks.text: You can also trigger this effect with a keyboard shortcut. Hold the Option key and click your mouse to activate the pointer instantly. To change the laser color, right-click on the slide during the show. Go to Pointer Options and pick your preferred color.
Adjusting your system-wide cursor on Mac

If you struggle to see your cursor, you can make it larger or change its color in macOS settings. These changes apply to every app, including PowerPoint. This is the best way to improve visibility while editing your slides.

items: Open the Apple menu and select System Settings.
Change the Pointer outline and fill colors to your preference.

blocks.text: These settings take effect immediately. You do not need to restart PowerPoint for the changes to show up. Use a high-contrast color like yellow or bright blue if you are presenting on a projector.
Sometimes the cursor behaves unexpectedly. It might disappear or show up on the wrong screen. Understanding these behaviors helps you stay calm during a live presentation.

items: Cursor disappearing: PowerPoint hides the cursor after a few seconds of inactivity. Simply move your mouse to bring it back.
Multi-monitor issues: macOS may display the cursor on both your laptop and the projector. This is a standard behavior and cannot be disabled in PowerPoint.
No laser pointer icon: Ensure you are in full Slide Show mode. The feature is often unavailable in Presenter View or during screen recordings.

blocks.text: If you require advanced features like custom cursor trails, clicks, or specific shapes, you might look at third-party tools. Apps like ScreenPointer allow for more control during screen sharing or live presentations. Always check the developer website for compatibility with your version of macOS before installing.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor shape in PowerPoint for Mac?
faq.answer: No, PowerPoint for Mac does not support custom cursor shapes. You can only use the default system cursor or the built-in laser pointer during a presentation.

faq.question: How do I make my cursor bigger for a presentation?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer and adjust the Pointer size slider. This will make your cursor larger in all applications, including PowerPoint.

faq.question: Why does my cursor disappear in PowerPoint?
faq.answer: PowerPoint automatically hides the cursor during a slideshow to keep the focus on your content. Move the mouse to make it reappear.

steps.text: Open System Settings, go to Accessibility, then Display, and move the Pointer size slider.
